title: ⚡ [Performance] Use Promise.all for concurrent reference updates in CMS service
body:
💡 **What:** 
Replaced the sequential `await` loop over `Object.entries(references)` with a concurrent `Promise.all` implementation in `removeReferences`, `addReferences`, and `create` methods within `integrations/cms/service.ts`.

🎯 **Why:** 
The previous implementation processed reference updates (I/O bounds) one by one in a `for...of` loop. Because these API calls/database updates are mutually independent, executing them sequentially forces the system to wait for each to finish before starting the next, wasting valuable execution time. Concurrently triggering them dramatically reduces overall response latency, especially when handling multiple references for items.

📊 **Measured Improvement:**
A baseline benchmark simulated the sequential I/O cost versus the parallel approach (using a 50ms mocked API latency):
* **Sequential Baseline:** ~202ms (for 4 reference groups)
* **Parallel Performance:** ~51ms (for the same 4 reference groups)
* **Improvement:** ~75% reduction in execution time for I/O bound multi-reference updates.
